result.summary: Offline synthesis of the traffic sounds per contract §1: new tools/audio/traffic_synth.py writes assets/audio/traffic/traffic_sounds.json plus nine seamless mono loops (16-bit PCM, 32 kHz, 2.954–3.031 s): car_petrol, car_diesel, car_sport, van_diesel, truck_diesel, bus_diesel, tires_car, tires_truck, air. Engines reuse engine_synth.py by import (subclass TrafficEngine, no copy): steady cruise in top gear at part load (petrol I4 2500/min @120, diesel I4 1900/min @120, sporty I6 with sport exhaust 3200/min @140, van diesel 2200/min @110, 12.8 l I6 truck diesel 1250/min @85 with twin-entry turbine and after-treatment silencer box, 10.7 l rear-engine bus 1300/min @90). Listener in the neighbouring lane (3.5 m to the side, 1.6 m high), so engine bay, intake and exhaust are all heard. Extra gear-rattle component for truck/bus. Component levels are calibrated K-weighted at the cruise point. Each engine loop is a whole number of working cycles, cut at the quietest crank phase; the end is blended into the start at the same point in the cycle with correlation-compensated weights. Tyres are synthesised circularly over the loop (periodic by construction): road texture excitation, tread blocks with pitch sequencing repeating each revolution, air pumping, horn amplification, cavity resonance split by rotation (car 218 Hz; truck 128–141 Hz over 12 tyres of three kinds with rib treads that 'sing'), road unevenness, slow surface variation. Air is a 3-band turbulent whoosh with slow gusts. All loops are normalised to −20 LUFS (K-weighted, BS.1770, ungated); relative levels come only from gain_db. Godot .import files are committed (PCM instead of the 4.7 default QOA, forward loop [0,N)) and verified in Godot (format, rate, loop_end = N). Seam checks: jump P9–P53, HF P23–P86, envelope step ≤ 0.47 dB, DC < 0.01 LSB. A Movie Maker recording of Godot's real looped playback shows nothing at the wrap points (P54–85, chance level). Output is bit-identical on re-run; player banks and engine_synth.py are md5-identical. New tools/audio/traffic_preview.py is a reference pass-by simulator (retarded-time Doppler with c = 343 m/s, 1/r and 1/r² for air, source size, equal-power pan, ISO 9613-1 air absorption) with 4 scenarios, measured checks, spectrograms, level/pitch plots and MP4s. Results: measured pitch matches exact Doppler within 0.31 % (car passed at +50 km/h: −7.7 %; sports car from behind: −9.3 %); left channel louder for a car on the left (+2.2 dB on approach, +13.9 dB at the pass); truck 2.7–3.4 LU louder than a car with a lower centroid (≈485 vs 606–680 Hz). German implementation section §4 appended to docs/verkehrsgeraeusche.md (model, parameters per sound, calibration, checks, regenerating, tuning, deviations). Tests: 273 unit + 9 integration checks, all passed.
deviations: gain_db changed from the contract table: truck_diesel +3.0 (contract 0.0), tires_truck +1.0 (0.0), bus_diesel 0.0 (-1.0). With the contract values a truck was only 0.6-1.5 LU louder than a car at the closest pass in the size-aware pass-by simulation (equal-loudness loops; the extended source and the car's air whoosh eat the difference); §3 requires 'hörbar lauter'. Physically a truck engine at 85 km/h is about 10 dB(A) louder than a car engine at 120 km/h from the roadside, tyres only 3-5 dB. Result: truck +2.7..3.4 LU, bus +2.3 LU over a car. Reverting means changing three numbers in SOUNDS in traffic_synth.py and regenerating. Documented in docs/verkehrsgeraeusche.md §4.10.

Extra informational top-level JSON block 'synth' (generator, loudness reference, per-loop measurements, component shares); all runtime fields, classes and models are exactly as in the contract apart from the three gains above.
Engine loop lengths are 2.954-3.031 s instead of exactly 3 s, because each holds a whole number of working cycles (within the 2-4 s range).

The WAVs already loop when loaded: the committed .import files set compress/mode=0 (PCM; Godot 4.7 default is QOA), edit/loop_mode=2 and edit/loop_end=N. The contract only says the runtime switches the loop on; doing it again at runtime is harmless.
notes_for_lead: Runtime hints, measured with Godot 4.7.2 Movie Maker: Godot plays [loop_begin, loop_end) and interpolates cleanly across the wrap. If the runtime sets the loop itself, use loop_end = data.size()/2, which is correct only for 16-bit PCM mono; never N-1 (that is what the importer's -1 default produces) and never with QOA, where data.size() is not a sample count.

Notes for the TrafficAudio agent (they are also in doc §4.7): (1) randomise each vehicle's start offset in the loop, since all vehicles of a class share one loop; (2) give the air layer a steeper fall-off with distance than engine/tyres and weight it by size, otherwise the car whoosh dominates the pass; (3) size-based near-field softening takes 1-3 dB off a truck at the pass; (4) with azimuth panning the L-R difference on the approach (vehicle 8-40 m ahead) is only about ±2 dB and 12-15 dB at the pass, so §3 test thresholds for 'louder on the left beforehand' should allow for small values; (5) loop peaks are -5.7 to -9.7 dBFS at -20 LUFS; with positive gains and near-field gain, keep headroom on the traffic bus.

Possible merge conflict: if the runtime branch created placeholder files or fixtures under assets/audio/traffic/, take these generated ones. After merging run godot --headless --import (tools/run_tests.sh does it); the .import files are committed with uids, and regenerating rewrites only [params].

Regenerate: python3 tools/audio/traffic_synth.py (~10 s, deterministic). Demos and checks: python3 tools/audio/traffic_preview.py --out DIR (~1 min; ffmpeg and ImageMagick needed only for media). --gain NAME=DB tries other balances without regenerating.

Nobody listened during development. Quality is backed by the measurements above (spectra against published tyre/road noise shapes, K-A balance, tonality, seams, Godot playback). The MP4s with a scrolling playhead are for the user to watch and listen to.

Kept as in the contract: police uses car_sport, and there is one shared 'air' loop for all classes (size is left to the runtime). No changes in scripts/; engine_synth.py and assets/audio/engines/* verified md5-identical.

result.summary:
The runtime for traffic sounds, the spatial siren and the room sound is built, tested and verified in Movie Maker recordings of the real game. Everything was developed with my placeholder loops: the synthesis agent's real sounds have not been heard or measured in the game yet.

- TrafficAudio (scripts/audio/traffic_audio.gd, pure maths without AudioServer):
  - Loading: reads traffic_sounds.json plus the WAVs and switches each loop on. It uses a copy of each WAV without a path, which works for PCM and Godot's default QOA import.
  - Vehicle class: taken from the sprite id (traffic/<model>_<colour>, police/<country>, unknown → car; unknown heavy vehicles → truck).
  - Distance and direction: measured to the nearest point of the vehicle body, so a long truck stays "beside" you while it is beside you.
  - Level: traffic_db + gain_db + speed term + distance law (reference distance × size; the air layer falls off faster, so the "whoosh" is only heard close by), faded out towards traffic_max_m.
  - Pan: constant power from the angle. Pitch: speed^pitch_exp × Doppler (relative speed along the line of sight, exaggeration factor 2) × ±6 % spread fixed per vehicle id. Air absorption: low-pass that drops with distance.
  - Voices: the 6 nearest vehicles get engine + tyres + air, with 25 % hysteresis and 0.3 s fades; a released slot is only reused once silent.
- Output: AudioStreamPlayer2D in an own invisible SubViewport world with an AudioListener2D. Godot ramps the per-channel gains, so pan and level changes do not click. Each voice has its own bus with a low-pass, sending to the Room bus.
- Siren: an extra voice at the police car (id -2) with pan, Doppler and its own distance law, with a minimum level so a chase from 320 m stays audible. set_siren() and hud_hints() still switch it; without the police car in the list it plays centred at the old level.
- RoomAudio (scripts/audio/room_audio.gd):
  - Room bus (to SFX) for engine, traffic and siren: two early reflections and a long tunnel reverb whose share fades in over 0.8 s when the camera enters a tunnel.
  - Engine bus (to Room): a short stereo reverb behind a high-pass gives the player's engine width while keeping it centred.
- AudioManager: new set_traffic(vehicles, listener), set_environment({tunnel}), traffic_state(), traffic_perf(). Traffic fades out on pause, after 0.35 s without calls and after the stage result; stop_all() silences it at once. A missing sound file means no traffic sound and no error. Debug flags: --traffic-sounds, --audio-config=k=v,..., --mute-bus, --perf.
- race_session.gd passes the renderer's car list, the chase camera and the tunnel state every frame.
- Config: audio.* keys with _doc_traffic/_doc_room. Docs: docs/ui.md "Audio" (new subsection with model, buses, measurements, tools) and ARCHITECTURE.md §11/§13/§14.
- Placeholders: tests/fixtures/make_traffic_fixtures.py writes 9 seamless loops plus a JSON in the contract format into tests/fixtures/traffic/ (16 kHz, 1.6 s, RMS -15 dBFS).
- shoot_vehicles.gd: new single-car `passby` scenario, `--audio-trace` CSV and AUDIO_PERF output.

Measured in Movie Maker recordings:
- Car passed on the left: left channel up to 9 dB louder while it is left, back to centre (0.1 dB) afterwards.
- Pitch drop at passing: fundamental 71.5 → 62.5 Hz (ratio 1.14, calculated 1.15); it follows the trace within ±1–2 %.
- Truck on the right: right channel 11–13 dB louder for about 1.2 s, peak 5.4 dB above the car, lower (63.8 → 52.1 Hz).
- Siren: passes on the left (up to 17 dB louder there); its 440 Hz tone goes 471 → 402 Hz, within 1.5 % of the trace.
- Tunnel: reverb fades in over 0.8 s; impulse response RT60 2.2–2.5 s, reverb about 2 dB below the direct sound; outdoors only the early reflections (−13.6 dB, no tail).
- Voice swap: no clicks or level jumps.
- Own engine in the real race: L/R correlation 1.000 before, 0.885 after, balance within ±0.3 dB.
- CPU: update() alone 0.05 ms for 41 vehicles and 0.09 ms for 161 (headless benchmark). In the rush-hour race recording, update plus pushing values to the players averages 0.23 ms per frame, under software rendering and Movie Maker.

Tests: 19 new unit tests (test_traffic_audio). tools/run_tests.sh: 292 unit tests and all 9 session checks pass.
deviations: Engine width: decorrelated delay taps (the suggested approach) were tried and rejected. Measured, they comb-filtered the harmonic engine differently per channel and pulled it up to 1.7 dB to one side depending on rpm. Instead the Engine bus has a short diffuse stereo reverb (audio.engine_width 0.6) behind a high-pass (audio.engine_width_hipass 0.1 ≈ 600 Hz), so the strong low harmonics stay mono and the image stays centred.

Voice choice: contract says 'nearest vehicles'. Trucks and buses (heavy flag) count 1.45× nearer when ranking, which is cheaper than a class lookup per vehicle. Class size is used for the reference distance as the contract specifies.

Doppler uses the relative speed along the line of sight (listener treated as at rest in the air), as the task wording says, not the two-speed moving-listener formula. The difference at these speeds is under 0.5 %.

Additions beyond the contract: siren minimum level while on (audio.siren_floor) so a far chase stays audible; nearest-point-of-body source model; Doppler smoothing over 80 ms; the air layer uses a fixed distance falloff of 2 (constant, not a config key).

'Finish' interpreted as the stage result: traffic stays audible during the finish roll-out and fades out once the session stops calling set_traffic after the result. The siren is switched off at the finish line as before.
Placeholder loops are 16 kHz / 1.6 s (contract: 32 kHz, 2–4 s) to keep the committed files small (about 460 KB). The runtime takes the rate from the WAV.

Measurement tooling (rec/analyse/f0track/clicks/width/spectrogram scripts, room impulse probe) stays in the scratchpad, not in the repo. Only the shoot_vehicles.gd additions (passby scenario, --audio-trace, AUDIO_PERF) and the AudioManager debug flags are committed.
notes_for_lead: Real assets: once assets/audio/traffic/ is merged, run `godot --headless --path . --import`. The default WAV import is QOA, which the runtime handles; commit the generated .import files. Then record once without --traffic-sounds to check levels with the real loops.

Level calibration: audio.traffic_db = -4 was tuned with placeholder loops normalised to RMS -15 dBFS. If the real loops are louder or quieter, change traffic_db by the difference, or have the synthesis agent normalise to RMS -15 dBFS. With the placeholders, a car beside you is about 3–4 dB above the player's engine in the near channel.
Without traffic_sounds.json the game only prints 'AudioManager: keine Verkehrsgeräusche (... fehlt)'; the siren, room sound and engine width still work.

Quitting while loops are still playing (e.g. --quit-after in recordings) prints Godot's 'ObjectDB instances were leaked at exit' warning. The unmodified game does the same with its engine and wind playbacks (3 instances in the baseline run, more now). The 'resources still in use' error that real loaded WAVs would add is avoided by using path-less copies. tools/run_tests.sh runs headless with no players, so it is unaffected.

Possible merge conflicts: config/game_config.json (I appended keys at the end of the audio section and edited audio._doc), docs/ui.md (Audio section, file table) and ARCHITECTURE.md (§11/§13/§14). I did not change docs/verkehrsgeraeusche.md, to avoid conflicts with the synthesis agent.

Tuning knobs, all in audio.*: traffic_listener_ahead_m 3 m (the passing peak lands as the car leaves the screen edge; 4–5 m would put it earlier), traffic_doppler 2, reverb_tunnel_wet 0.3, engine_width 0.6 (0 = mono), traffic_voices 6.

To reproduce the measurements: tests/race/shoot_vehicles.gd -- --scenario=passby|overtake|overtake_cars|police|tunnel together with --write-movie X.avi --fixed-fps 30 --no-shots --traffic-sounds=res://tests/fixtures/traffic/traffic_sounds.json --audio-trace=X.csv [--mute-bus=Engine]. Do not mute SFX: the Room bus sends into it. The analysis scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/passby/runtime/.

Timing figures from parallel Movie Maker runs are inflated by CPU contention with software rendering (the engine shows 0.9–4 ms there instead of its documented 0.25–0.44 ms). The clean numbers are the headless benchmark (0.05–0.09 ms for update) and solo runs (0.14 ms with 2 cars, 0.23 ms in rush hour).
